Contents: I was not aware of PimEyes before class today. One ethical concern of facial recognition tools that are accessible to the public is the potential for anyone to breach a person's privacy by finding images of them that they were unaware of. While this might not have much implication for the average civilian, perhaps for Goverment officials and those who require good standing to remain in their position this could pose the threat of another angle of attack for opponents looking to blackmail or paint them a certain way. This could of course also be a valid threat for anyone not working in such areas.
